title: Real-Life Money Maths: Loans, Inflation, Percentages
subject: math

sections.body: INFLATION means prices rise over time, so money buys less. With 5% inflation, something costing 100 costs about 105 next year.
Loans charge interest. The APR (annual percentage rate) includes fees, so it's the fairest number to compare loans by.
Percentage change = (new − old) ÷ old × 100. A price going from 80 to 100 is a 25% increase.
Minimum payments on a credit card can make a debt last years and cost far more than the original amount.

quiz.q: A phone's price rises from 200 to 250. What's the percentage increase?
hints: Divide the change by the ORIGINAL price.

quiz.q: Which number is best for comparing the true cost of two loans?
hints: One number includes interest AND fees.
Comparing cars by total price (not just the deposit) is fairer. Which loan number is like the total?
quiz.explain: APR includes interest and fees, so it's the fairest comparison.
